title: Does the interior affect terminate on the image too? Vasquez: only the exterior mark does
source_text: LIV. Rursus ergo quaeritur, An quum imago & exemplar simul uno eodemque actu adorationis coluntur, utraque pars istius actus, id est, tam interior submissionis affectus, quam ejus nota exterior, non ad solum exemplar, sed ad imaginem quoque pertineat, atque terminetur? Et quidem Vasquez, conformiter fundamento ab eo posito, existimat, quum Imago & exemplar simul adorantur, solam exteriorem notam submissionis ad imaginem pertinere, atque ad eam terminari; interiorem vero submissionis affectum circa solum exemplar versari, & illud solum respicere. Nam Capite septimo saepius dictae Disputationis 108, ex variis Conciliorum & Patrum testimoniis manifeste colligi dicit, unam eandemque adorationem esse imaginis, & exemplaris, non sicut quidam Theologi putant, sed ita ut unus sit affectus submissionis, qui in solum exemplar feratur: nota autem exterior illius, solum imaginem respiciat, & per illam ex affectu illo submissionis, cogitatione, & desiderio, in ipsum exemplar transmittatur.
pass_a_gloss: Again therefore it is asked, When the image and the exemplar are cultivated together by one and the same act of adoration, whether each part of that act, that is, both the interior affect of submission and its exterior mark, pertains also to the image and is terminated there, not only to the exemplar? And indeed Vasquez, conformably to the foundation laid down by him, judges that when Image and exemplar are adored together, only the exterior mark of submission pertains to the image and is terminated in it; but that the interior affect of submission is conversant about the exemplar alone, and regards that alone. For in chapter seven of Disputation 108 so often named, from various testimonies of Councils and Fathers he says it is manifestly gathered that there is one and the same adoration of image and of exemplar, not as certain Theologians think, but so that there is one affect of submission which is carried into the exemplar alone: but that its exterior mark regards the image alone, and through it from that affect of submission, by thought and desire, is transmitted into the exemplar itself.
pass_b_english: Follow-up: when one act covers both, does the interior affect terminate on the image too?
Vasquez: only the exterior mark terminates on the image; the interior affect aims at the exemplar alone, and the mark is transmitted to it (disp. 108, c. 7).

choices.why: Exterior mark passes honor through to the exemplar.
